book.title: Hillbilly Elegy: A Memoir of a Family and Culture in Crisis

argument.statement: America’s problem is generational neglect, leaving white working classes abandoned and later condescended to, leading to breaking point.

book.rationale: This book is primarily a personal account of the author's life and experiences growing up in a struggling community, making Memoir & Autobiography the dominant subject, with Society & Culture as a secondary subject due to its exploration of cultural and social issues.
book.summary: THE INTERNATIONAL BESTSELLER Coming November 2020 as a major motion picture from Netflix starring Amy Adams and Glenn Close 'The political book of the year' Sunday Times 'A frank, unsentimental, harrowing memoir ... A superb book' New York Post 'I bought this to try to better understand Trump's appeal ... but the memoir is so much more than that. A gripping, unputdownable page-turner' India Knight, Evening Standard J. D. Vance grew up in the hills of Kentucky. His family and friends were the people most of the world calls rednecks, hillbillies or white trash. In this deeply moving memoir, Vance tells the story of his family's demons and of America ' s problem with generational neglect. How his mother struggled against, but never fully escaped, the legacies of abuse, alcoholism, poverty and trauma. How his grandparents, 'dirt poor and in love', gave everything for their children to chase the American dream. How Vance beat the odds to graduate from Yale Law School. And how America came to abandon and then condescend to its white working classes, until they reached breaking point.
